src/data/featureConfig.js + tests/featureConfig.test.js. Design calls made here that .2/.3/.5 inherit: (1) heightFt THROWS for wall/box rather than defaulting — a zero-height wall renders as nothing in an elevation, the exact silent failure 'reject loudly' exists to catch; a surface may not carry a heightFt at all. (2) Absent file == empty list: normalizeFeatures(null|{}) -> {features: []}, no 'declares no features' throw, so an empty POST in .5 is valid. (3) normalize/serialize are exact inverses ({features} both ways, no projectId echo); the round-trip is tested as normalize(serialize(normalize(x))) deepEqual normalize(x), since serialize drops defaults. Both directions read one defaultStyle(type) table. (4) Only the geometry key matching the type is emitted — footprintFt for surface/box, pathFt for wall — so projection in .2 cannot read the wrong one. (5) style.fill/stroke restricted to hex, a colour name, or none, since they land in SVG attributes and arrive over an endpoint in .5. Also added projectFeaturesPath() and loadFeatures(); featuresFile in projectPaths.js is left to .5.

src/render/featureProjection.js + tests/featureProjection.test.js (projectFeature dispatches; projectFeatureToPlan/ToElevation do the work). All four compass directions are pinned by absolute expected pixels, not only by mirror parity, so a bug shared by both sides of a pair cannot hide. Design calls .3 inherits: (1) The axis span is taken in PIXELS after axisToX, never in feet — on a mirrored view the larger axis value gives the smaller x, so a min/max in feet puts the rectangle's left edge on its right. (2) TWO degenerate silhouettes are legitimate, not errors: a surface has height 0 by definition, and a wall seen end-on (a fence running away from the viewer) has width 0. The renderer must draw both at strokeWidthPx or a fence vanishes in two of four elevations. (3) depthFt reports {min,max,near,far}; near/far come from orientation.farIsHigh so compareElevationDepth composes with the plant sort. BUT near is NOT a sufficient sort key on its own: a house spanning y 12..20 sorted at near=12 draws in front of a plant at y=15 that stands inside its footprint. Single-key sorting cannot be right for an extended footprint — .3 has to split or clamp. (4) closed=false for wall only; closing a fence would fill in the yard behind it.

src/render/featureViews.js (shapes), src/render/elevationOrder.js (the combined sort), + wiring in topView/elevationViews/renderViews and tests/featureViews.test.js. tests/topView.test.js and tests/elevationViews.test.js pass UNMODIFIED; 37/37 e2e. Design calls: (1) Plants and features go through ONE comparator with ONE depth accessor — a parallel per-kind expression is how features silently sort at depth 0, pinned to the very back or very front, which looks almost right. The test asserts the straddle order AND notDeepEqual against the depth-zero ordering. (2) An extended footprint is drawn WHOLE at its nearest edge, no splitting: correct for a box (nothing is planted inside a house), and the one case it gets wrong is a wall running away from the viewer, which is edge-on and therefore a hairline. (3) Bands: 0 = surface (flat, so it is ground and draws beneath every plant), 1 = plants and wall/box, 2 = the pre-existing Callirhoe force-front, moved verbatim from elevationViews. (4) SVG draws neither a zero-width nor a zero-height rect AT ALL, so both degenerate silhouettes become a <line> at stroke weight — without that a surface and an end-on fence are simply invisible. (5) No data-name on feature groups: styles.css gives '.view svg [data-name]:hover' a pointer cursor, and features are not interactive until .6, which hit-tests data-feature-id.

Fetching features.json straight off disk is NOT viable at boot: Chrome logs the network 404 to the console itself, before any try/catch runs, and tests-e2e/app.spec.js:26 asserts boot is console-clean. That was caught by running the e2e suite. loadFeatures' 404-to-empty branch is now only for pure static-file mode.

server.js GET+POST /api/features, featuresFile in projectPaths.js, loadProjectFeatures/persistFeatures in src/data/persistence.js, boot wiring in app.js, tests/persistFeatures.test.js (5) + tests-e2e/features.spec.js (5, own scratch project 'features-save'). Full unit suite passes; 42/42 e2e. DEPLOYED and verified live: 'docker compose restart web' then curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/features?project=backyard' -> {"features":[]} HTTP 200. Design calls: (1) There is a GET twin, not just the POST the bead asked for, and the app loads through it — fetching features.json off disk logs a console 404 on every load of every project that has never drawn a feature, which app.spec.js:26's console-clean assertion catches. featureConfig.loadFeatures is now static-file-mode only. (2) Missing file reads as {features: []}; a file that exists but is unreadable still throws — absent is normal, corrupt is a fault. (3) POST refuses a body with no features[]: absent means 'this is not a feature list', not 'no features', and accepting it would erase the whole yard model with no history to recover from. An explicit empty array IS accepted — that is how the last feature goes. (4) The response is re-normalized on the client: the drawing reads style and heightFt off every feature, and a response is trusted no more than a file. (5) The e2e containment test posts a body naming a different project and asserts the named one is untouched — worth noting normalizeFeatures never reads raw.id at all, unlike normalizeProjectConfig, so there is no id scrub; the test pins that rather than assuming it. PNG export needed no work: viewCapture.js clones the live SVG (cloneNode + serializeToString), so features come along free. persistFeatures has NO UI caller yet by design — nl-avt.6 owns that. Docs: AGENTS.md gained a 'Yard features' section and CLAUDE.md was mirrored per the repo rule. Non-blocking for .6: app.js passes no status callback to loadProjectFeatures, so a corrupt features.json degrades to an empty yard with only a console.warn — the author sees no features and no reason why.

src/render/featureOverlay.js (pure geometry: handles, hit-test, drag resolution, new shapes, reorder), src/interaction/featureController.js (pointer), src/interaction/featurePanel.js (list + form), plus a fourth mode in app.js/index.html/styles.css. tests/featureOverlay.test.js (9) + 3 UI tests in tests-e2e/features.spec.js against their own scratch project 'features-edit'. Full unit suite passes; 45/45 e2e with every pre-existing spec UNMODIFIED. No deploy needed: server.js is untouched and src/index.html/styles.css come off the bind mount.

Design calls: (1) A FOURTH mode, not a modifier on Setup. setRuler is a modifier on one gesture; feature editing has its own selection state and would have made three consumers competing for pointerdown on one SVG. applyMode decides every lock state in ONE place so exactly one kind of controller is ever unlocked. (2) Feature controllers are built ONLY for plan panels (null for elevations, index alignment kept) — a controller on an elevation would be a consumer that never unlocks. (3) Handles are drawn in EVERY plan view, not just one selected view. That differs deliberately from Setup mode's one-view rule: setup edits a single view's geometry, features edit a model shared by all of them, so editing from a detail crop is coherent. The pointer goes through transform.viewBoxToPlan, so a drag in a crop still writes YARD feet — unit-tested. (4) createFeatureShape gives a new wall/box a real heightFt. normalizeFeatures refuses one without a positive height, and the first frame of a new fence must not be what trips a guard meant for malformed files. (5) applyFeatureEdit normalizes the candidate DIRECTLY rather than serializing first — a freshly added shape has no style yet, and normalizeFeatures is what supplies one. (6) NO auto-save: features are setup like project.json, per this epic's own framing, so Save features is explicit. A plant drag auto-saves; this deliberately does not. (7) The panel got its OWN BEM block (feature-panel__*). Reusing setup-panel__* made four existing e2e specs fail on strict-mode ambiguity — two panels, one class name, and a selector for one silently matches the other. styles.css carries both hooks on every shared rule so the visual language stays single-sourced.

Known limits, none blocking: a polygon collapsed to zero area cannot be re-picked on canvas (pickFeatureAt ignores the touch radius for polygons, using pointInPolygon) — the panel list is the escape hatch. Type is not editable on an existing feature: surface/box are a polygon and wall is a path, so switching would need the footprint rebuilt; delete and re-add. Vertices can be dragged but not added or removed, so a bed stays a quadrilateral — worth its own bead if curved beds matter. nl-jfm updated: svg.style.cursor now has three writers.

Reported rather than repaired. resolveYardConflicts (src/render/yardBounds.js) returns each primary elevation whose axis range does not intersect the plan's; app.js shows it in #projectNotice at boot. For example-frontyard: 'View "west" covers y 0–14.3 ft, but the plan covers 14.8–45.1 ft — nothing in the yard can appear in both.' The geometry itself is NOT rewritten: the correct coordinate is one the author has to choose and the app cannot measure it, so guessing would silently move someone's yard. resolveYardBounds keeps its silent fallback on purpose — a drag needs some bound — the conflict is now surfaced alongside it. 2 unit tests in tests/yardBounds.test.js, including that end-to-end touching is not overlapping. Note the app's own touch-action/cursor precedent: this is the same shape of bug, a silent fallback that looks like it worked.

NOT REPRODUCED as a code defect, and now pinned by tests so it cannot become one silently. tests-e2e/setupSave.spec.js drives a scratch copy of example-frontyard's exact geometry (plan origin {2, 14.83}, north originFt.y -7.14, west -3.20) through: a plain Save views; a form edit on the plan then Save; a form edit on an elevation then Save; and a ground-line handle drag then Save. Every origin round-trips untouched, and the drag moves ONLY the dragged view's origin. The pure round trip normalizeProjectConfig -> serializeProjectConfig -> normalize is stable too, verified separately.

So the flattening was almost certainly a real Setup-mode handle drag: dragging an elevation's ground line to the panel's bottom edge sets originFt.y to exactly 0, and serializeProjectConfig then omits an origin of {0,0} — the tool working, leaving a file that looks like it never had an origin.

The residual risk is real but different from what this bead assumed, and is NOT a serialization bug: view geometry has no undo (project.json keeps no history, deliberately — see nl-avt.5 and persistProjectConfig's comment), so one stray handle drag plus a Save silently destroys a calibrated ground line with no way back. Worth its own bead if it bites again; the cheap mitigations are a confirm on Save when an origin goes to zero, or keeping the previous project.json as a single .bak on write.
